newsitem.title: UK: British output prices rise 0.5 percent in December.
newsitem.headline: British output prices rise 0.5 percent in December.

text.p: British output prices, a key indicator of future inflation, rose 0.5 percent in December for a 1.7 percent year-on-year increase, official data showed on Monday.
This compared with no change in the month to November, when the year-on-year increase was 2.1 percent.
Input prices fell 0.5 percent seasonally adjusted for a 5.9 percent year-on-year fall. This compared with a 2.9 percent monthly drop in November for a 5.2 percent year-on-year decline.
The data was in line with analysts' expectations and the Treasury said core cost pressures remained very subdued.

Finance minister Kenneth Clarke meets Bank of England governor Eddie George on Wednesday and George is expected to press for an increase in interest rates from 6.0 percent because of his concern over growing inflationary pressures.

Sterling weakened on foreign exchange markets after the output price figures, which traders said gave ammunition to Clarke, who will be reluctant to raise rates shortly before an election, due by May.

"Clarke probably has the option after today's numbers and last week's of delaying a rate rise a little," said Kit Juckes of Natwest. "It's still very difficult to see how he can avoid a rate rise this side of an election."
